_comment: Resources that must NOT be migrated autonomously. BLOCK entries are skipped entirely by the planner and plan-native-migration skill. WARN entries require explicit human approval before any ticket is created.

severity_levels.BLOCK: Never migrate autonomously. Resource is a singleton, causes account-wide impact, or creates irreversible state that cannot be safely isolated to a test run.
severity_levels.WARN: Migrate only with human review and extra safety gates. Resource is sensitive (shared infra, billing, DNS, audit trail) but can be isolated with care.

blacklisted_resources.reason: Singleton — one per AWS account. E2E tests would overwrite the account alias, affecting all users.
Singleton — one per AWS account. Changing or deleting the password policy affects every IAM user in the account.
Service-linked roles are auto-created and managed by AWS services (EKS, RDS, etc.). Deleting one breaks the dependent service account-wide; a test instance cannot be isolated from production use.
Singleton per contact type (BILLING/OPERATIONS/SECURITY) per account. Overwriting a contact silences account-level security or billing notifications for the entire account.
Controls region opt-in/opt-out. Opting out of an active region terminates all workloads running there, including potentially the pipeline host itself.
Account-wide public access block (one per account). Disabling it would expose ALL S3 buckets in the account to public access.
Account-wide toggle (one per region). Disabling encryption-by-default removes the encryption guarantee for ALL new EBS volumes across the account.
Singleton per region. Changing the account-default KMS key causes all subsequent EBS volumes to be encrypted with a different key, breaking key-management expectations account-wide.
Singleton per region — every account has exactly one default VPC. Deleting or modifying it breaks default networking for all resources that rely on it (including potentially the pipeline host).
Singleton per VPC. Modifying the default security group rules can block or expose all instances placed in the default SG.
Singleton per VPC. Modifying the default route table breaks routing for all subnets not explicitly associated with a custom route table.
Singleton per Availability Zone within the default VPC. Deleting it removes the default launch target for that AZ account-wide.
Singleton per VPC. Modifying DHCP options changes DNS server and domain settings for all instances in that VPC.
Singleton per VPC. Modifying the default NACL changes traffic rules for all subnets not explicitly associated with a custom NACL.
Singleton per account per region (AWS enforces exactly one). Re-creating it during a migration cycle drops compliance recording continuity for the entire account.
Controls the singleton configuration recorder (start/stop). Stopping the recorder during migration pauses all compliance checks account-wide.
Singleton per account per region. Only one delivery channel may exist; re-creating it during migration interrupts the flow of compliance snapshots.
Singleton per account per region. Deleting and re-creating the detector during migration disables threat detection for the entire account and loses all existing findings.
Account-level SecurityHub enablement (singleton). Deleting it disables SecurityHub for the whole account, removing all security findings and standards subscriptions.
Singleton per account. Configures cross-region finding aggregation; re-creating it during migration causes a gap in cross-region security visibility.
Account-level Macie enablement (singleton). Deleting it disables Macie and loses all sensitive data findings for the account.
Account-level Inspector v2 enablement. Disabling Inspector removes vulnerability scanning for all EC2 instances and container images in the account.
Singleton per account per region. Deleting the graph disables Amazon Detective and destroys the behavior graph, losing all investigation history.
Singleton per account (imported using the registry ID = account ID). Overwriting it removes cross-account pull access for all consumers of the registry.
Singleton per account per region (imported using registry ID). Re-creating resets the account-wide scanning rules and scan-on-push settings.
Singleton per account per region (imported using registry ID). Only one replication configuration exists; re-creating it interrupts cross-region/cross-account image replication.
Account-level ECS service settings (awsvpc trunking, container insights, etc.). Changing the default affects every ECS cluster and task in the account.
Account-level singleton. The administrator list and cross-account settings control ALL Lake Formation access. Misconfiguration or deletion locks out the entire data lake.
Singleton per region. Holds the account-level CloudWatch role ARN and default throttling settings for all APIs in the region; re-creating removes logging from every API.
Singleton per account per region. Changing encryption settings affects all X-Ray trace data storage for the account.
Account-level singleton. Controls whether cross-account backup is enabled; re-creating resets the setting for the entire account.
In compliance mode, vault locks are IRREVERSIBLE — even AWS Support cannot remove them within the lock period. Accidentally locking the wrong vault with wrong retention periods is unrecoverable.
Singleton per account per region. Toggling serial console access off would break emergency recovery access for ALL EC2 instances in the region.
Singleton per account per region. Only one Spot Instance data feed subscription may exist; re-creating it during migration causes a gap in spot interruption logging.
The AWS Organization itself — the ultimate singleton. Deleting it dissolves the organization and removes all member accounts from the org structure. Completely irreversible.
Creates and optionally closes real AWS member accounts. Closing an account triggers a 90-day suspension period; this cannot be treated as a throwaway test resource.
Singleton per SSO instance (IAM Identity Center). One set of ABAC attribute mappings per instance; re-creating drops attribute-based access control for all permission sets.
Deleting or reparenting OUs breaks SCP and tag-policy inheritance chains for all accounts under them.
SCPs, tag policies, and backup policies apply across multiple accounts. A misconfigured SCP can lock every account out of critical AWS actions.
Attaching or detaching SCPs to accounts/OUs is immediately effective across all accounts in scope.
Delegating admin access to a member account grants cross-account management privileges for an AWS service.
Core shared network infrastructure. Deleting a Transit Gateway disconnects all VPC attachments and on-premises connections routing through it, potentially taking down the pipeline host.
Direct Connect gateway is the shared network backbone for on-premises connectivity. Deleting it terminates all associated virtual interfaces.
VPN gateway attached to a VPC. Detaching or deleting breaks site-to-site VPN tunnels for the VPC.
Manages AZ opt-in/opt-out. Opting out of an AZ that contains running resources (subnets, RDS, EKS nodes) will break those resources.
Public hosted zones: deleting a zone or replacing its NS records breaks DNS resolution for the domain globally. Can take the entire pipeline down if the domain hosts the cluster API endpoint.
DNSSEC misconfiguration (e.g., removing the KSK without updating the parent DS record) causes complete DNS resolution failure for the zone.
Modifies the VPC-level DNS resolver behavior. Misconfiguration breaks name resolution for all instances in the VPC.
Deleting an active trail breaks audit and compliance logging. Organization trails affect all member accounts and cannot be re-created without a gap in the audit log.
Holds persistent audit event data. Deleting an event data store is irreversible and destroys the event history.
Account/region-level Data Catalog encryption settings (one per region). Changing the encryption key affects all Glue catalog operations in the region.
Account-level Glue catalog resource policy. Replacing it removes cross-account Glue access for all consumers.
Account-level default patch baseline per OS type (one per OS per region). Changing it alters patch behavior for all managed instances using the default baseline.
Account-level SSM service settings (e.g., default S3 bucket for Session Manager logs, Parameter Store throughput tier). Some settings incur costs or change security posture account-wide.
Account-level SNS SMS preferences (spending limit, default sender ID, report delivery). One set per account; changing the spending limit can disable SMS for the entire account.
Singleton per account per region — only one receipt rule set can be active. Changing the active set re-routes all inbound email for the account.
Account-level CloudWatch Logs resource policy. Removing or overwriting it revokes cross-service write permissions (e.g., Route53 query logging, API Gateway access logs).
Cost budgets enforce spending limits. Deleting a budget removes the associated alerts and automated actions, disabling cost controls for the account.
Automated cost control actions (e.g., stop EC2 instances when over budget). Deleting removes the guardrail; replacing with incorrect thresholds may stop production workloads.
Cost and Usage Report definition. Deleting causes a gap in billing data delivery; downstream consumers (cost analytics, FinOps tooling) will fail.
Account-level cost anomaly detection monitor. Deleting removes anomaly alerts for the account.
Account-level IoT device indexing configuration. Re-creating it triggers a full device re-index for the account, which can take hours and temporarily breaks fleet indexing.
Account-level IoT Core logging configuration (one per account). Changing or deleting it alters logging verbosity and log destination for all IoT resources.
Region-level AWS Backup settings (one per region). Controls which services are opted into backup; re-creating can disable backup for entire service categories.
Account-level service quota adjustments. Reducing a quota below what currently-running resources consume will break those resources and prevent new ones from being created.
Account-level SageMaker ServiceCatalog portfolio status. Disabling it removes the SageMaker portfolio from AWS Service Catalog for the entire account.
Global network topology container. Deleting it removes all registered devices, sites, links, and transit gateway registrations attached to it.
